subject: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks

Team —

Quick pulse as we hit the middle of the quarter. Overall progress is decent, but two initiatives are consuming runway and risking QBR commitments: Realtime routing improvements and Model variant rollout testing. I think we need to tighten scope and surface dependency asks to keep the quarter deliverable.

Proposed scope adjustments (high level):
- Realtime routing: pause A/B of the multi-region experiment; focus on first-priority latency path and telemetry for this quarter.
- Variant rollout testing: reduce test matrix to top 3 models + 1 quant profile; defer long-tail combinations.

Immediate asks (owners & dates):
- Karthik: provide revised infra capacity estimate (GPU-hours/week) for the reduced routing scope — by Thu 9/16.
- Marissa: update launch checklist and stakeholder list for the trimmed rollout — by Fri 9/17.
- Vanessa: confirm which SLAs we can relax for the canary (latency SLO vs. availability) and impact on customers — by Fri 9/17.
- Ben: coordinate with Acme on the integration timeline; ask Sarah for a revised mutual action plan — Sarah, can you confirm a firm date for the joint test window?

Attachment: priority-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix and suggested cuts).

We should aim to finalize decisions in the next 48 hours so we can bake this into the QBR pack. Short comments inline are fine — if we need a 20m sync, I can grab a slot.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks

Alex —

Thanks for the clear options. I support narrowing the realtime routing experiment to a single latency path for this quarter; the multi-region split will require more infra and OOM risk.

A couple quick notes:
- If we relax latency SLO for the canary, we should lock availability and error-budget alerts so customers aren't surprised.
- I can take point on communicating the scope change to CS leads — I’ll draft a short FAQ.

One ask back: can Karthik give a low/high capacity range instead of a single number? That’ll help decide if we can keep a tiny multi-region burst window in week 12.

On the Acme side, Sarah — happy to take a 15m to align on the joint test window.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 08:12 AM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick pulse as we hit the middle of the quarter...

Quick technical response: we can reduce the routing scope as suggested. Preliminary capacity delta for the trimmed plan:
- Low (conservative): 120 GPU-hours/week (we hold more cache in RAM, smaller batch windows)
- High (optimistic): 200 GPU-hours/week (if we keep a small burst/secondary-region window)

Notes / caveats:
- The optimistic window requires enabling cross-region KV cache warmup; that has a 48–72h warmup and additional storage cost.
- If we defer the long-tail quant profiles, we should schedule a follow-up for the regression harness (Marissa) so we don’t lose coverage.

I’ll follow up with exact cost delta and a short table by Thu 9/16 EOD.

— Karthik
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:44:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks

Alex / team —

Thanks for the update and the concrete asks. Acme is comfortable with the reduced joint test surface as long as we get a clear mutual action plan and a fixed 2-week window for integration testing before the end of the month.

I’ve attached a short slide deck with our preferred test matrix and proposed dates (acme-integration-slides.pdf). We can commit to the window of Sep 27–Oct 8 if Redwood confirms capacity and a single contact.

Ben — assigning to you to coordinate the DocuSign and MSA amendment, procurement looped in CC.

— Sarah Lopez
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly pulse: priority shifts, scope adjustment, dependency asks

Appreciate the quick reactions. Summary / decisions: 

1) Scope: realtime routing experiment will be reduced to single latency path for Q3 deliverable. Multi-region burst deferred to Q4 unless Karthik’s optimistic capacity is confirmed and funded.
2) Testing matrix: we will limit variant rollout to top 3 models + 1 quantization profile. Marissa to update checklist by Fri 9/17.
3) Capacity: Karthik to send low/high GPU-hour numbers by Thu EOD (9/16) — he has this in flight.
4) Acme: agreed mutual test window Sep 27–Oct 8; Ben to own the contract amendment and DocuSign.
5) Communications: Vanessa to draft customer-facing FAQ; I’ll add an internal note to the QBR pack with the adjusted roadmap.

Action owners & near-term deliverables:
- Karthik: capacity numbers and cost delta (Thu 9/16 EOD).
- Marissa: updated launch checklist + regression schedule (Fri 9/17).
- Ben: DocuSign/contract path & Acme point-of-contact (Tue 9/21).
- Vanessa: FAQ draft and CS sync note (Fri 9/17).

I uploaded the final priority matrix and a living decision tracker to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-quarterly-pulse — please add updates as you complete tasks. I’ll include a one-slide summary in the QBR pack by next Wed.

If anything changes materially, call it out in-thread. Otherwise let’s execute to these commitments.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
